input.question: Do satellites generally have on-board computers, and what are they like?
input.ground_truth: Yes. Modern satellites couldn't function without computer processors on them. Generally CPUs on satellites are well behind those on the ground in terms of performance, however they are built to resist the effects of cosmic radiation (I'm not sure precisely how). There is also the factor that satellites take a long time to design and build, meaning that when they launch their computers are no longer cutting edge by spacecraft standards, never mind compared to Earth-based chips. For example in 1997 the PowerPC 750 was released, a CPU that powered many Apple computers of the era including the first iMac. In 2001 a radiation-hardened version, the RAD750, was developed but the first spacecraft to use a RAD750 didn't launch until 2005. It's gone on to be used in about 150 spacecraft including the Curiosity rover. A modern smartphone CPU would offer hundreds of times the performance, but a modern smartphone CPU couldn't reliably withstand the high radiation and temperature swings in outer space.
